subject: Service-account egress identity & FQDN assertions for private endpoint deployment

From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@greenfieldlabs.com>

Cc: ops@greenfieldlabs.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service-account egress identity & FQDN assertions for private endpoint deployment

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We are finalizing our network checklist for the private deployment (VPC, on-prem connector) and have a couple of specific asks from compliance: they need a formal assertion of the egress identity for the Redwood control plane and guidance for an FQDN-based allowlist tied to a service account identity.

Concretely we need:
- A template that states the public FQDNs/hostnames Redwood control plane will call (for telemetry, model fetches, licensing checks).
- An audited assertion of which service account(s) or client identity will originate traffic (we prefer service-account level rather than per-instance IPs).
- Guidance on whether IP ranges will be stable / ephemeral and recommended TTL for allowlists.
- Attach any existing template or evidence you can provide (CSV or spreadsheet preferred).

We attached our internal "network_requirements_v2.docx" for context. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports TLS SNI based fingerprinting and if mTLS will be required for the control-plane callbacks?

Thanks,
Alice Moreno
Sr. Infrastructure Security Engineer
Greenfield Labs

Attachments: network_requirements_v2.docx (docx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@greenfieldlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service-account egress identity & FQDN assertions for private endpoint deployment

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. I've reviewed your doc and sketched a practical approach below; attaching a short template (egress_assertion_template.csv) you can use to record the final FQDNs / assertion statements.

Short summary / options:
1) Service-account identity (recommended): Redwood can assert egress origin at the service-account level for control-plane interactions when the customer uses our private connector. We provide a signed assertion (timestamped) showing the service-account id and the scope of callbacks. This maps cleanly to your compliance ask.

2) FQDN allowlist vs IP allowlist:
   - FQDN (preferred): Less brittle; we provide the list of FQDNs and a recommended verification method (DNS A/AAAA + TLS SNI + expected cert CN).
   - IP (possible): We can provide ephemeral NAT ranges for a rolling window (daily rotation). If you need long-lived static IPs, we can evaluate a dedicated egress pool but that requires a Reserved Capacity order.

3) mTLS and SNI: Redwood supports mTLS for control-plane callbacks. We also support TLS SNI fingerprinting as an additional signal but we treat SNI as advisory — mTLS is the stronger control and preferred for high-sensitivity environments.

Attachment: egress_assertion_template.csv (CSV) — fill the FQDNs and intended ports.

Next steps (proposal):
- You fill the template with the FQDNs you allow for runtime (we can propose default FQDNs for model fetches / telemetry).
- We produce a signed assertion (PDF) with service-account id and a list of endpoints + validity window.
- If you require static IPs beyond a rolling ephemeral pool, we can scope a dedicated egress assignment (procurement required).

Do you want us to phone into your compliance call on Wednesday to present the assertion format?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Karthik — this looks good. Quick clarifications from compliance: they prefer service-account assertions + FQDN allowlist. They also want the assertion to include TTL guidance and evidence of IP ephemeral rotation if IPs are used.

We attached our formal requirements doc (greenfield_requirements.docx) — section 2.1 spells out the evidence format (CSV / signed PDF + hash). Can you confirm whether the signed assertion will include a cryptographic signature we can verify (public key / fingerprint)? Also: what logging/headers will Redwood include for callbacks so we can reconcile requests in our outbound firewall logs?

If possible, Marissa or David — can someone join our compliance sync on Thursday 10:00 AM PT?

Thanks,
Alice

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@greenfieldlabs.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service-account egress identity & FQDN assertions for private endpoint deployment

Hi Alice / team — looping through our legal & infra responses and confirming next steps ahead of Thursday's sync.

What we will provide:
- Signed assertion PDF (cryptographic signature using Redwood's platform key, plus public fingerprint) listing: service-account id, allowed FQDNs, allowed ports, TTL window, rotation cadence for ephemeral IPs (if used).
- FQDN guidance spreadsheet (attached: egress-fqdn-assertions.xlsx) with suggested hostnames grouped by function: telemetry, model fetch, licensing, metrics.
- Firewall rule recommendations (high level):
  * Outbound only (no inbound): allow TCP 443 to listed FQDNs.
  * Block port ranges except explicitly allowed (eg block 25, 445).
  * Prefer FQDN + DNS allowlist; if you must use IPs, accept a rolling NAT pool with daily rotation and a 48-hour TTL window for reconciliation.
  * Require mTLS for control-plane endpoints; if mTLS is not available, require SNI + cert CN verification and IP allowlist fallback.
  * DNS TLS (DoT/DoH) is allowed; if you inspect TLS, use SNI as secondary check only.

Logging & headers we will emit (for reconciliation):
- X-Redwood-Service-Account: <service-account-id>
- X-Redwood-Request-Id: <uuid>
- Timestamp (ISO8601) + Signed assertion reference id

Action items / timeline:
- Today: Karthik will generate the signed assertion template and examples (we already attached the template).
- Thu 10:00 AM PT: Compliance sync — Marissa and David will join to confirm signature verification process.
- By Fri COB: Deliver sample signed assertion and the finalized FQDN spreadsheet.

If you have any policy constraints that force static IPs longer than 7 days we need to know immediately, otherwise we'll proceed with the ephemeral NAT pool option.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Partnerships — Redwood Inference
